beats.text: This is me on the twenty eighth of the month. I have eleven dollars and three bills and a brain that feels like a browser with forty tabs open.
And right here I'm about to make a decision I would never make on payday.
I'm about to borrow three hundred dollars from a store with a neon sign.
And here's the weird part. I'm not stupid. Being broke is making me stupid.
By the end of this video you'll know why being broke steals your brainpower and the one small thing that gives it back.
But most people scroll away before that part. And honestly if you're broke right now that's exactly what your tired brain wants to do.
So let me tell you about my twenty eighth. Rent is due on the first. The phone bill is due tomorrow. And my car makes a noise like a sad duck.
I'm at work but I'm not really at work. My body is typing an email. My brain is doing math. Rent minus phone minus gas minus food. It never adds up.
Me at work pretending to listen in a meeting.
My boss asks me a simple question. I say yes. I have no idea what I just said yes to.
And at lunch I skip eating to save eight dollars. Then at four I'm so hungry I buy a fourteen dollar snack box from the vending machine.
That's the math of a tired brain. Save eight. Lose fourteen. Feel proud for three hours.
On the way home I forget my keys in the car. I forget to reply to my mom. I forget it's my friend's birthday. I'm forgetting everything except the number in my bank account.
It's like my brain has one parking spot and the bills took it. Everything else drives around in circles.
Then I see a letter on the counter. The electric bill. It was due five days ago. It's been sitting there the whole time. I walked past it every day.
Me walking past the bill I'm scared of.
Late fee. Thirty five dollars. Which I don't have. So now I'm more broke because I was too broke to think.
That's the loop. And you've probably been inside it too. Broke makes you forget. Forgetting makes you more broke.
And that's when I walk past the store with the neon sign. Cash today. No credit check. And for the first time in my life it looks like a good idea.
My phone buzzes. A text from the bank. Low balance. Like I needed a reminder. Like my stomach wasn't already reminding me.
Payday me would laugh at that sign. Twenty eighth me walks right in.
Payday me versus twenty eighth me.
So that night I start wondering. Am I just bad with money? Is something wrong with me?
And then I found a study that changed how I see all of this. Scientists went to farmers in India who grow sugarcane.
Not lazy people. Not careless people. Hard working farmers who wake up before the sun.
These farmers get paid once a year. At harvest. So right before harvest they're broke. And right after harvest they have money.
Imagine getting your whole salary once a year. You'd be a millionaire in October and eating rice in August.
Same farmers. Same people. Same brains. The scientists gave them puzzles before harvest and again after harvest.
Guess what happened. Before harvest when they were broke they did worse. After harvest they did better. The only thing that changed was the money.
My brain before payday versus after payday.
Then the same scientists tried it at a mall in New Jersey. They asked people to imagine their car needs a repair.
When it was a cheap repair everyone did fine on the puzzles. When it was an expensive repair the people with less money suddenly did a lot worse.
And the people with more money? They did the same no matter which repair. A big bill didn't scare them. So it didn't slow them down.
They didn't even have to pay for anything. Just thinking about the money problem was enough to make their brains slower.
The researchers said it was like losing a whole night of sleep. Every single day. Just from money worry.
Me trying to make smart choices on zero sleep and eleven dollars.
To be fair some later studies found smaller effects and scientists still argue about how big it is. But the main idea keeps coming back. Worry takes up space.
Think about your phone. Ten apps running in the background. It gets hot. It gets slow. It dies at fifty percent. That's your brain on money worry.
It's not that you're dumb. You're running too many apps.
Me at the end of the month trying to remember my own phone number.
And there's a second thing that happens. Scientists call it tunneling.
When you're broke your brain zooms in on the emergency right in front of you. Rent. Tomorrow. Now. And everything outside the tunnel just disappears.
It's like a firefighter who only sees the fire in front of him. Great at putting out that fire. Doesn't notice the house next door is starting to smoke.
It's like looking through a toilet paper roll. You can see one thing really clearly. And you can't see the giant truck coming from the side.
Me solving this week's problem by creating next month's problem.
That's why the neon sign looked good. Inside the tunnel I only see three hundred dollars today. I don't see what I'll owe in two weeks.
And the tunnel is not just loans. It's buying the cheap shoes that break in two months. It's paying the minimum. It's the rent-to-own couch that costs triple.
Every one of those makes sense inside the tunnel. And every one of them makes the tunnel longer.
Payday loans are built for the tunnel. Fast. Easy. One page. Because they know a person in the tunnel won't read page two.
The payday loan guy when I walk in on the twenty eighth.
And when the loan comes due I'm broke again. So I borrow again. The tunnel gets longer. It's a hamster wheel with interest.
Me every two weeks.

beats.text: Remember my video about being broke three days after payday? This is the brain part of that story.
And here's what hit me the hardest. Rich people make dumb money mistakes too. They just have room for them.
A rich guy forgets a bill and the late fee is a rounding error. He doesn't even notice. I forget a bill and it becomes my whole week.
Think about a pilot. Bad weather? A good plane has extra fuel. A plane with an empty tank has to land anywhere. Even in a field.
Same mistake. Different damage.
It's like two people walking on a cliff. One has a fence. One doesn't. They both trip the same amount. Only one of them falls.
So when someone says poor people just make bad choices? Put them in the tunnel for a month. Let's see their choices.
People who never had a money problem explaining money problems.
Being broke isn't a personality. It's a weight on your back while you're taking a test.

card.t: It's a weight. Not a personality.

beats.text: So how do I get out? Willpower? Nope. Willpower lives in the same brain the bills are eating.
The answer scientists keep pointing to is one word. Slack. A little room. A little space between you and the cliff.
Quick reminder this is education and not advice. But here's how I started building mine.
First a tiny emergency fund. Not six months of salary. Just enough so a flat tire isn't a disaster. Even a few hundred dollars changes how your brain feels.
Start stupidly small. Five dollars a week. Put it somewhere boring. Don't touch it. In a year that's a flat tire you can survive.
The first time I had two hundred dollars I wasn't planning to spend I slept like a baby. For real. My brain finally closed a few tabs.
Me with a two hundred dollar emergency fund.
Second I automated my bills. Every bill pays itself on payday. So the twenty eighth me never has to remember anything. Payday me already handled it.
My bills paying themselves while I sleep.
Let smart you make the decisions so tired you doesn't have to.
Third I moved my savings to a different bank. One I don't see in my app every day. Out of sight. Out of the tunnel.
It's like hiding cookies on the top shelf. You can still get them. You just have to really want them. And at eleven at night you usually don't.
Fourth I made big money decisions only on payday. Never on the twenty eighth. The twenty eighth me is not allowed to sign anything.
Twenty eighth me trying to sign up for anything.
And fifth I cleared the junk. Every little subscription and every tiny decision I didn't need. Fewer things to juggle means more brain left over.
Me deleting eleven apps that each wanted four dollars a month.
And then something cool happened. With a little slack my decisions got better. Better decisions gave me more slack. The loop started spinning the other way.
Six months later I opened every letter the day it arrived. I even answered my mom on time. She asked if I was sick.
That's the whole secret. You don't need a smarter brain. You need an emptier one.
And that's where investing comes in later. Money that grows quietly is the biggest slack there is. But you build the fence first. Then you build the tree.
And the cool part? Once you have slack you finally have the brainpower to learn the stuff nobody taught you. Like how investing actually works.
So remember the one small thing. A tiny cushion. Not to get rich. To get your brain back.
If you're in the tunnel right now you're not lazy and you're not dumb. You're carrying a weight. Put a little bit down every month.
Broke isn't who you are. It's where you are. And you can leave.
Oh and that neon sign store? I walked past it last week. On the twenty eighth. Didn't even slow down.
Next time I find out why school taught me the Pythagorean theorem but never once told me how a credit card works.
Subscribe. It takes one click. Even on the twenty eighth.
